verdict.rationale: PayPal publishes its US commercial rates (Checkout 3.49%+, cards 2.99%+, Pay Later 4.99%+, plus an international surcharge), and the evidence frames these as the rates agent-initiated orders inherit. That lets a merchant estimate agentic-channel costs without contacting sales. However, the page explicitly has no separate agentic/AI-channel fee schedule, and agentic commerce services are form-gated with onboarding by the AI team. missing for 10: an explicitly published fee schedule for agent-originated transactions, documented confirmation that standard rates apply to Store Sync/Agent Ready (Braintree) agentic orders, and published Braintree agentic pricing.

support.subject: As a merchant, the fees for agent-originated transactions are published — I can price agentic channels without asking sales

citations.quote: The published US commercial rates that agent-initiated orders inherit: "PayPal Checkout" and "PayPal Guest Checkout" at "3.49% +" fixed fee
No separate agentic/AI-channel fee schedule is published on the page.
